1.explanation: AccordionItem calls the shared internal hook useId('accordion-item') to auto-generate its panel ID. Footer’s mobile nav groups (in @carbon/react) also use the same useId implementation with the same default or hard-coded prefix, resulting in duplicate IDs. To resolve the issue, useId must accept a customizable prefix or the AccordionItem (and Footer) must expose an idPrefix prop so each consumer can namespace its generated IDs and avoid collisions.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering a page that includes both carbon-components-react’s AccordionItem and @carbon/react’s Footer, each library uses the same internal useId counter and default prefix, so elements in the footer nav (which under the hood render as accordion-style groups) end up generating IDs like “accordion-item-1”, colliding with the IDs generated by the AccordionItem on the page. The screenshot shows two <div> panels both having id="accordion-item-1", flagged as an accessibility error.

2.explanation: The root of the duplicate-ID bug is the shared auto-ID generation logic and hardcoded prefixes in two separate packages. The hook useId (in useId.js) and the helper uniqueId (in uniqueId.js) both produce sequential IDs using the same default prefix logic. AccordionItem (in AccordionItem.js) calls useId('accordion-item') with a fixed prefix, and the Footer component in the IBM.com library likely does the same under the hood. Because these modules each maintain their own counter but share the same prefix, IDs collide when used together. To fix this, useId should accept an optional prefix override prop (and propagate that through AccordionItem), ensuring that AccordionItem and Footer can be configured with distinct prefixes, preventing collisions.
2.bug_scenario: On a page that renders both Carbon’s AccordionItem (from carbon-components-react) and the IBM.com Footer (from @carbon/ibmdotcom-react), the auto-generated IDs collide (e.g. both render elements with id="accordion-item-1"). In the DevTools accessibility checker you can see the error “The <div> element has the id "accordion-item-1" that is already in use.”
